guidance.Low: Normal behaviour. Background logging and routine monitoring; no escalation.
guidance.Moderate: Something unusual is happening. Assign an analyst, check disclosure (SEBI) obligations and draft a holding statement.
guidance.High: Strong, company-specific stress. Start the executive crisis protocol: legal review, investor-relations alert and a real-time PR response.

criteria.name: Market reaction
criteria.question: Did the share price fall more than the market and its sector can explain?
criteria.how: From the previous 6 months we learn how each stock normally moves with the NIFTY 50 and with its sector peers. We subtract the move they explain; what is left is the company-specific (abnormal) return. We add it up over the last week and the last month and divide by the stock's usual day-to-day noise to get a z-score — so a 5% drop counts for more in a calm stock than in a jumpy one, and a sector-wide sell-off does not count.
criteria.scale: 0 down to −1σ (everyday noise) · 50 at −2σ (~2% chance) · 100 at −3σ or worse

criteria.name: Trading stress
criteria.question: Is the stock being traded unusually nervously?
criteria.how: Compares the last 10 days' volatility with the previous 90 days, and the last 5 days' volume with the previous 60 days. Spikes mean investors are reacting to something. If the stock is actually beating the market this week, the spike is likely good news, so it only counts for a quarter.
criteria.formula: C2 = ½·clip((vol ratio − 1) ÷ 1.5) + ½·clip((volume ratio − 1) ÷ 2), ×0.25 if beating the market
criteria.scale: 0 at normal activity · 100 when volatility is 2.5× and volume 3× normal while falling

criteria.name: Lingering damage
criteria.question: Has company-specific damage built up and stayed?
criteria.how: Adds up the company-specific (abnormal) returns day by day into a performance line, then measures how far that line now sits below its best point of the last 3 months. This is damage that has not recovered yet. Some gap is always normal, so it is measured in units of the stock's usual 3-month wobble (σ × √63).
criteria.scale: 0 up to 1σ (normal) · 50 at 2σ behind (~5% chance) · 100 at 3σ or more behind

criteria.name: News tone
criteria.question: How negative is the recent opinionated coverage?
criteria.how: Every relevant headline from the last 7 days gets a sentiment score from −1 to +1 and a recency weight (halving every 72 hours). Over the opinionated headlines (negative or positive — routine neutral news does not water a crisis down) we take the weighted average negativity, adding 2 imaginary neutral headlines so one stray story cannot spike the score. With no headlines this is 0 and the score rests on the stock.
criteria.formula: C4 = 100 × Σ wᵢ·max(0, −sᵢ) ÷ (Σ wᵢ + 2)   over non-neutral headlines
criteria.scale: 0 with no news or only positive news · ~40 for a few clearly negative stories · →100 for many

criteria.name: Negative coverage
criteria.question: How much negative coverage did the company get in the last 7 days?
criteria.how: Adds up the recency weights of the headlines labelled negative — a measure of how loudly and how recently the bad news was carried. The first few stories matter most and it levels off, because ten stories about the same issue are not ten times worse than one.
criteria.formula: C5 = 100 × (1 − e^(−Σ wᵢ over negative headlines ÷ 5))
